title: Credit-card application and eligibility
overview: A credit card provides a borrowing facility with repayment terms rather than direct access to a savings balance. Eligibility, supporting documents and approval depend on the issuer's assessment; general guidance is not an approval decision.
procedure: In the fictional application flow, select the card category and review the configured document checklist with a demo agent. Application status is account-specific and requires demo verification; no approval or real credit limit is promised.

title: Credit limits and available credit
overview: Available credit can differ from the total credit limit because of posted balances, pending authorizations, fees or repayments awaiting posting. A limit increase involves issuer assessment and is not guaranteed by a payment history alone.
procedure: A verified demo profile may view its configured total and available credit. For a limit-review enquiry, an agent explains the synthetic review workflow; the assistant does not approve lending or encourage borrowing beyond the customer's means.

title: Billing cycles, statement and due dates
overview: A billing cycle groups card activity into a statement period. The statement date closes that period, while the payment due date is the repayment deadline shown on the statement; purchases near a cutoff can appear in a later cycle.
procedure: Use the synthetic card statement to check the cycle and due date after profile verification. Confirm payment posting rather than relying only on a transfer receipt; real deadlines must come from the issuer's current statement.

title: Minimum due and total card amount due
overview: The minimum amount due is a required partial payment, not a promise that no interest will accrue. Paying only that amount can leave a balance subject to the card's terms; the total amount due represents the statement obligation.
procedure: After demo verification, the adapter can read configured synthetic minimum and total dues. Review the card's published terms before deciding how to repay; the assistant explains concepts without prescribing a personal repayment strategy.

title: Credit-card repayment and late payment
overview: Card payments may take time to appear in the issuer's record depending on the channel. A late or insufficient payment can attract charges and affect repayment status under the agreement; an initiated transfer is not always a posted repayment.
procedure: For the synthetic workflow, check due date, payment reference and posting status before raising a missing-payment case. Only configured fees may be quoted; no automatic waiver, reversal or credit-report correction is promised.

title: Credit-card interest and cash advances
overview: A cash advance is borrowing cash against a card facility and may have different fees and interest treatment from a purchase. Carrying a purchase balance can also attract interest according to the issuer's calculation method.
procedure: Consult the configured synthetic card schedule for an example of the applicable charge categories. The assistant will not invent a real interest rate or estimate personalized borrowing costs without the necessary statement terms and inputs.

title: Credit-card EMI and reward programmes
overview: Converting an eligible card purchase into installments changes its repayment structure and may involve charges. Reward points follow a separate programme with earning, expiry and redemption rules; not every transaction is necessarily eligible.
procedure: In the demo, ask an agent to review a synthetic purchase for EMI eligibility or inspect the fictional rewards record. Read the configured offer before confirming any conversion; the assistant cannot redeem real rewards or promise approval.

title: Credit-card replacement and closure
overview: Closing a credit card is different from replacing its physical card or freezing new transactions. Outstanding balances, installment plans, recurring payments and rewards may need attention before a closure request can be completed.
procedure: The fictional closure checklist asks a demo agent to review dues, linked mandates and unresolved disputes. A lost or stolen credit card should be reported urgently through the security workflow rather than waiting for ordinary closure review.

title: Reward expiry and missing reward points
overview: Reward programmes may post points after a delay, exclude particular transactions or expire unused points under their terms. A reversed purchase can also lead to points being adjusted, so compare the transaction and reward records.
procedure: For the synthetic review, identify the relevant fictional purchase and statement period, then ask a demo agent to compare the reward schedule. The assistant cannot reinstate real expired points or promise an exception to programme rules.
